steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Refining means making specific, deliberate improvements — not just running the piece again but fixing identified problems. | Key Fact: Timing and pacing: the speed at which moments unfold — too fast loses impact, too slow loses engagement. Every pause must be earned. | Key Fact: Transitions: how you move between scenes — clumsy transitions break the theatrical experience. Make them part of the drama. | Key Fact: Consistency: every performance must be at the same level — energy, focus and delivery must be reliable and repeatable.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the difference between rehearsing and refining? Why is refinement essential? | Describe how you would ensure smooth transitions between scenes in a devised piece. | How can pacing and timing affect the audience's experience of a key dramatic moment?
